meta.title: Unit 2, Day 1: Shop Safety
meta.subtitle: Study guide. Everything on today's certification exam is on this page.

sections.blurb: What today is and how to use this page
sections.title: Start here

blocks.content:
Follow along with this while we go through it in class. **Everything on today's certification exam is on this page.**

You do not have to take notes. This is yours to read and keep. If you want to add anything, write it in your engineering notebook next to the section it goes with.

You will not have this during the exam.

### What Unit 2 is

You will run five machines and make one part on each. The five parts assemble into a shop trophy that you keep.

Before you touch any machine, you have to be cleared. That is what today is for.

sections.blurb: PPE, and what to do when you get hurt
sections.title: 1. Foundations

blocks.content:
### Eye protection

Safety glasses go on any time you are in the shop area. Not just when you are running something.

You do not have to be the one cutting to catch something in the eye.

### Hair, clothing, jewelry

Long hair tied back. Loose clothing tucked in. Jewelry off.

Anything that hangs can get pulled into a machine. Being careful does not help once something is caught.

### Respirator

Some jobs in this unit require one. Everyone owns their own and brings it to the next class.

A respirator only works if it seals against your face. If it feels loose, it is not protecting you. Fix it before you start the job, not in the middle of it.

### Reporting injuries

Every injury gets reported when it happens. Tell Mr. Pina.

That includes the small ones. The ones that barely bleed still get reported.
Take your notes for this section in your engineering notebook.

sections.blurb: Who is allowed to run a machine, and when
sections.title: 2. Clearance

blocks.title: Nobody runs a machine until they are cleared
blocks.content:
There are two parts to getting cleared:

1. Pass this exam.
2. Get cleared by Mr. Pina at the machine, after you watch that station's video.

Watching the video is one half. The clearance is the other half. Feeling ready is not the same as being cleared.
Until you are cleared, you stay with your group in a role that does not involve running the machine: deburring, measuring, or writing the station record.

### Never work alone

No running machines in an empty shop. That includes open shop outside class.

If something goes wrong, there has to be someone there.

### When you are not sure

If you are not sure whether something is safe, stop and ask.

Trying it slowly to see what happens is still trying it.
Take your notes for this section in your engineering notebook.

sections.blurb: The three rules that matter most
sections.title: 3. At the machine

blocks.content:
### Know the emergency stop before you start

On every machine, find the emergency stop before you turn it on.

If you cannot stop a machine fast, you are not ready to start it.

You will see the emergency stop again in each station's video, at the machine, before you use it.

### Nothing goes into a running machine

Stop the machine first. Every time. That includes your hands.

If something is in the way, do not wait to see whether it clears itself.

blocks.title: If something changes, stop
blocks.content:
A new sound, a new smell, or a new vibration means something changed.

Stop the machine and tell Mr. Pina. Do not finish the cut first.

Stopping costs you a minute. Finishing the cut can cost you the part, the tool, or your hand.
Take your notes for this section in your engineering notebook.

sections.blurb: Safety is not only about your own machine
sections.title: 4. Other people

blocks.content:
### Do not distract someone who is operating

No tapping them on the shoulder. No asking them something mid-cut.

Wait until they are finished.

### Speak up, any group, any machine

If you see someone about to do something unsafe, say something before they start.

It does not matter whose station it is or whose group they are in. Waiting until after they finish is waiting until it is too late to matter.

### Horseplay near a running machine

Tell them to stop. If they do not stop, tell Mr. Pina.

It puts everyone nearby at risk, not just the person doing it.
Take your notes for this section in your engineering notebook.

sections.blurb: How you leave it, and whose machine is whose
sections.title: 5. The room

blocks.content:
### Leave the area usable

Clean your station every day, even if it makes you late.

The next person has to be able to work there. Leaving your mess makes your problem into someone else's problem.

A cart comes around at the end of every class to collect work that is not finished.

### Machines are assigned during class

Every machine belongs to a group during the block.

If you finish early, stay at your station and start your notebook entry. Not another group's machine, and not a computer.
Take your notes for this section in your engineering notebook.

sections.blurb: How it works and what happens if you miss one
sections.title: The exam

blocks.title: You must get every question right to pass
blocks.content:
If you miss one, you retake it.

You cannot run any machine in this class until you pass and Mr. Pina clears you.

- No devices, no notes, no talking.
- If you have to retake it, that happens at lunch today or at the start of the next class.
- Read every question all the way through. Some of them are testing whether you are paying attention, not whether you memorized something.

Everything on the exam is on this page.

sections.blurb: One thing, and you cannot be in the shop without it
sections.title: Bring next class

blocks.title: Your respirator
blocks.content:
The 3M 7500 with the 60926 cartridges. Everyone needs their own.

Without it you are not in the shop.
